name: Pi extension ecosystem research for minimal Atlas config

description: Baseline Pi extension ecosystem research using pi.dev catalog and GitHub/web search sources

asi.hypothesis: Pi package catalog downloads plus GitHub/web search signals give a better popularity signal than GitHub stars alone.
asi.notes: autoresearch.md referenced by system was missing; initialized autoresearch.jsonl in current directory. Research is informational; no benchmark overfitting involved.

description: Expand Pi ecosystem research with flow-specific extension categories and package quality signals

asi.hypothesis: Targeted searches by workflow category (browser automation, markdown/content, safety/permissions) improve coverage for Atlas flow profiles beyond generic popularity rankings.
asi.new_findings: Notable flow-specific candidates: pi-agent-browser-native / pi-agent-browser / @victor-software-house/pi-agent-browser for browser automation; pi-markdown-preview for marketing/docs/content; pi-lens and permission packages for code quality/safety; pi-depo may be relevant to declarative profile installs.
asi.issue_creation: Subagent created GitHub issues #2-#7 for /atlas-flow and marketing, SSG/SSR, video, UI/UX, infra/IPsec/pentesting flows.
asi.overfit_guard: Metric is source coverage only; recommendations still need qualitative filtering for minimal global install surface and security review.

description: Validate declarative profile manager approach for minimal Atlas flow installs

asi.hypothesis: A declarative profile manager may be better than global LazyPi-style installs for Atlas because it preserves a tiny baseline while enabling on-demand flow bundles.
asi.new_findings: pi-depo is purpose-built for Pi packages/skills/extensions/MCP with kit.yml, ratings, disabled entries, profiles, diff/status/verify, and gist sync. It has ~5.8K downloads/mo and small package size, but pd sync also self-updates pi and reconciles orphans, which is powerful but too invasive unless used carefully. agentdeps and agentmux are broader cross-agent alternatives but less Pi-native for extensions. LazyPi remains best as catalog/bootstrap, not profile state manager.
asi.recommendation_shift: For /atlas-flow, implement local Atlas-owned flow manifests first; optionally support pi-depo export/import later instead of making pi-depo core global dependency.
asi.overfit_guard: Coverage metric increased from additional independent source categories; qualitative recommendation avoids simply maximizing package count/downloads.

description: Validate concrete package candidates for Atlas flow manifests

asi.hypothesis: Atlas flow manifests should classify packages by runtime invasiveness, not only downloads: low-footprint command/preview tools can be global-or-flow, while hook-heavy tools should stay on-demand.
asi.new_findings: pi-agent-browser-native is a strong browser automation candidate for UI/UX, marketing QA, SSG/SSR QA, and video workflows; it is well documented and redacts sensitive data, but requires upstream agent-browser and optional ffmpeg. pi-markdown-preview is strong for marketing/blogging/SSG docs; has 11.3K/mo downloads, but requires pandoc and Chromium for terminal previews. pi-lens is popular and powerful at 17.1K/mo but hook-heavy: intercepts write/edit, can auto-install many tools, autoformat, run LSPs, and enforce read-before-edit; recommend only project/flow opt-in, not Atlas global. pi-skill-palette is tiny, no deps, and may support minimal global workflow by explicit skill injection, though low downloads (317/mo) and older publish date mean trial before adopting.
asi.recommendation_shift: Add manifest metadata fields: install_scope=global|flow|project, invasiveness=low|medium|high, external_deps, auto_mutates_files, registers_tools, intercepts_write_edit. Use these to prevent high-invasiveness packages like pi-lens from becoming default global installs.
asi.overfit_guard: Did not rank by downloads alone; downgraded pi-lens globally despite high popularity because behavior conflicts with minimal/controlled Atlas baseline.

description: Validate domain-flow strategy: authored skills over niche Pi packages

asi.hypothesis: For marketing, video, UI/UX consulting, and infra/IPsec/pentesting, the Pi ecosystem likely has few mature domain-specific extension packages; Atlas should compose generic tools with Atlas-authored skills/prompts rather than hunt for niche packages.
asi.new_findings: Searches for SEO/marketing, video creation/editing, UI/UX design, and pentest/IPsec/infrastructure surfaced mostly generic workflow packages, web access, subagents, pi-agent-flow, safety guards, and noisy/irrelevant catalog hits. Heart of Gold Toolkit is the main broad skill bundle with relevant Guide content engine skills (blog/LinkedIn/content pipeline) and Babel Fish media skills (audio/image/visualize/linkedin carousel), but installing the whole package adds 32 skills and Pi-native commands; better to selectively install or borrow patterns after review.
asi.recommendation_shift: Flow manifests should separate tools from domain playbooks. Tools: browser, web access, markdown preview, subagents, maybe media generation. Domain expertise should live in Atlas-owned skills/templates: SEO audit, content calendar, SSG launch checklist, video script/storyboard/edit checklist, UI/UX heuristic audit, IPsec/pentest rules-of-engagement and report template.
asi.overfit_guard: Did not force package adoption where search evidence was weak; rejected popularity-by-association and kept domain logic in auditable Atlas text.

description: Validate /atlas-flow command implementation path in Pi docs

asi.hypothesis: The /atlas-flow installer should be a tiny Atlas-owned extension command rather than only a prompt template, because it must inspect manifests, prompt/confirm, and run package installation or settings edits.
asi.new_findings: Pi prompt templates are excellent for domain playbooks and accept argument hints/positional args, but only expand prompts. Extensions can register commands via pi.registerCommand, use ctx.ui for confirm/select, and run logic. Pi package docs confirm pi install defaults to global settings; -l writes project .pi/settings.json and project packages auto-install on startup. Package object filters can load only selected extensions/skills/prompts/themes, which is important for broad packages like Heart of Gold or tmustier bundles. pi-prompt-template-model can add model/skill/thinking behavior for command-like templates, but it still is not an installer.
asi.recommendation_shift: Implement /atlas-flow as a low-invasiveness global extension in Atlas. Keep domain playbooks as prompt templates/skills. Command UX: list/status/install/remove/diff/doctor; default to project-local installs (-l) for flow packages; require explicit --global for global installs; write/preview manifest-derived package filters; support dry-run first.
asi.overfit_guard: Chose the mechanism based on Pi capability boundaries, not popularity. Avoided converting everything into an extension: playbook text remains prompts/skills where simpler.

description: Validate safety model for Atlas flow package installation

asi.hypothesis: Because Pi packages run with full system access, /atlas-flow needs explicit safety gates: pinning, project-local defaults, filters, dry-run, and package review metadata.
asi.new_findings: Pi docs explicitly warn packages have full system access; npm version specs and git refs pin and skip package updates. pi install -l writes project-local settings and project installs land under .pi/npm or .pi/git. Package filters can narrow resources loaded from broad packages. Temporary trials with pi -e allow testing without persistent settings. pi-agent-browser-native has explicit redaction/security design but depends on external agent-browser. pi-lens confirms high-invasiveness behavior: write/edit interception, autoformat/autofix, LSP/tool auto-installs, and should require explicit flow/project opt-in.
asi.recommendation_shift: Atlas flow manifests should include security fields: pinned_source, source_reviewed_at, trust_level, permissions_summary, external_binaries, network_access, secret_handling, install_default=project, allow_global=false by default, requires_confirmation for high-invasiveness packages. /atlas-flow install should show a risk summary and require confirmation for any extension registering tools, intercepting writes, or auto-installing binaries.
asi.overfit_guard: Safety recommendation intentionally penalizes popular/high-capability packages when they broaden attack surface; not optimizing for maximum feature count.

description: Validate Atlas repo-fit and concrete flow manifest placement

asi.hypothesis: A concrete /atlas-flow design should match atlas-config's stow-managed minimal repo layout instead of adding another external package manager or broad global package bundle.
asi.new_findings: atlas-config README states the repo intentionally starts small, cherry-picks needed items, and stows pi/.pi/agent to ~/.pi/agent via just up. Existing Pi settings currently include many LazyPi-like packages globally (mcp, subagents, ask-user, web-access, memory, plan, simplify, add-dir, prompt-template-model, claude-cli, themes, usage, todo, btw, autoresearch, plannotator, slopchop, powerbar, raw-paste, interactive-shell, ralph, etc.), which conflicts with the desired minimal global surface. Existing custom Pi extensions are simple TS files under pi/.pi/agent/extensions, so /atlas-flow fits naturally there. There are many existing skills under pi/.pi/agent/skills, so domain playbooks can use the same stowed skill structure.
asi.recommendation_shift: Place flow manifests in pi/.pi/agent/flows/*.json or *.yaml, the installer command in pi/.pi/agent/extensions/atlas-flow.ts, and domain skills under pi/.pi/agent/skills/atlas-*/SKILL.md. Add a follow-up cleanup plan to reduce current settings.json packages to a small core baseline and move optional packages into flow manifests. Candidate manifest shape: id, description, packages[], skills[], prompts[], externalDeps[], safety{}, installDefaults{}, verification{}; package entries include source, pinnedSource, filters, scopeDefault, invasiveness, trustLevel, reason.
asi.overfit_guard: Grounded design in actual repo layout and current settings rather than abstract ecosystem popularity. This may reduce installed package count even though the research metric rewards more source coverage.
